**Surat ash-Shu'ara' (The Poets)**

Meccan, except for four verses at the end of the surah, from His saying ﴿And the poets—the deviators follow them﴾.

We have been related from Ibn Abbas that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "I was given Ta-Ha and the Tawasin from [al-Lawh al-Mahfuz (the Preserved Tablet)]."

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

* *

﴿Ta-Sin-Mim﴾. Hamzah, al-Kisa'i and Abu Bakr recited ṭasm, ṭas, ḥam and yas with a kasra on the ṭā', the yā' and the ḥā'. The people of Medina recited between the fatḥa (open vowel) and the kasra (the vowel *i*). The others recited with a fatḥa, for tafkhim (emphatic pronunciation). Abu Ja'far and Hamzah made the nūn in yas clear before the mīm of ṭasm, while the others pronounced it with ikhfa' (concealment). It is related from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, that he said: "Ṭasm: the scholars have been unable to explain it." Ali ibn Abi Talhah al-Walibi related from Ibn Abbas that it is an oath, and it is one of the names of Allah the Exalted. Qatadah said: it is a name of the Qur'an. Mujahid said: it is a name of the surah. Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi said: Allah swore by His majesty, His loftiness and His dominion [[The word "Allah" is omitted in manuscript "A".]].

[[The discussion of the disjointed letters (al-huruf al-muqatta'ah) at the beginnings of the surahs has already been given earlier; see above: 1/58–59. Ibn Kathir set out the opinions on the disjointed letters, the scholars' differences in interpreting them, and the wisdom behind their mention, and he dismissed what the evidence does not support. He said: "Others said: rather, these letters were mentioned at the beginnings of the surahs in which they occur to demonstrate the inimitability (i'jaz) of the Qur'an, and that creation is incapable of producing its like, especially since it is composed of these disjointed letters with which they converse. Al-Razi related this view in his Tafsir from al-Mubarrad and a group of verifiers. Al-Qurtubi related something similar from al-Farra' and Qutrub. Al-Zamakhshari affirmed it in his Kashshaf and defended it most thoroughly. Shaykh al-Imam al-Allamah Abu al-Abbas Ibn Taymiyyah adopted this school, as did our shaykh al-Hafiz Abu al-Hajjaj al-Mizzi, who related it to me from Ibn Taymiyyah." See: Tafsir Ibn Kathir: 1/36–39.]]

﴿Those﴾, i.e., these verses, ﴿are the verses of the Clear Book﴾.

**Verses 3–4:**

﴿Perhaps you will kill yourself with grief﴾: destroying yourself, killing yourself. ﴿That they will not be believers﴾: meaning, if they do not believe. This was when the people of Makkah denied him, and it weighed heavily on him, for he was eager for their faith. So Allah revealed this verse.

﴿If We wished, We could send down upon them a sign from the sky, and their necks would remain humbled before it﴾. Qatadah said: If Allah wished, He would send down upon them a sign by which they would be humiliated, so that none of them would turn his neck toward disobedience to Allah. Ibn Jurayj said: Its meaning is: If Allah wished, He would show them a matter of His command, after which none of them would commit an act of disobedience.

As for His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He, ﴿khadi'in﴾ (humbled, masculine plural), and He did not say *khadi'ah* (feminine singular), which would agree with the attribute of the necks (*a'naq*, feminine). On this there are several opinions. The first: He meant the owners of the necks; He omitted "the owners" (*al-ashab*) and placed "the necks" (*al-a'naq*) in their stead, because when the necks are humbled, their owners are humbled. So He gave the verb first to the necks, and then made *khadi'in* apply to the men. Al-Akhfash said: He returned the humbling (*al-khudu'*) to the pronoun that the necks were attributed to. Some people said: He used the masculine form of the attribute because it was adjacent to the masculine noun, which is His saying "*hum*" (they), following the Arabs' habit of masculinizing a feminine noun when it is attributed to a masculine one, and feminizing a masculine noun when it is attributed to a feminine one. It was also said: He meant "then they would be humbled (*fa-zallu khadi'in*)," and He expressed the whole body by the neck, as in His saying: ﴿That is because of what your hands have sent forward﴾ [al-Hajj: 10], and ﴿We have fastened his bird of omen to his neck﴾ [al-Isra': 13]. Mujahid said: By "the necks" He meant the leaders and the elders, that is, their elders would be humbled. It was also said: By "the necks" He meant groups, as one says: "The people came *'unuqan 'unuqan*," meaning in groups and companies. It was also said: He said *khadi'in* only to agree with the verse endings (*ru'us al-ay*), so that they would be in one pattern.

Al-Tabari (19/62) said: "The most preferable of these opinions, and the most consistent with what the commentators of the Qur'an have said, is that the necks are the necks of men, and the meaning of the sentence is: their necks would be humbled before the sign that Allah sends down upon them from the sky. And His saying *khadi'in* is masculine, because it refers to the *ha'* and *mim* (the pronoun 'them') in *a'naquhum*. This is like the verse of Jarir: 'I see the passing of years has taken from me, as the night-traveller takes from the crescent.' For if *marr* (passing) were removed from the sentence, what remains would still convey its meaning, and the removal would not corrupt the meaning of the sentence as it was before. Likewise, if *al-a'naq* (the necks) were removed from His saying 'fa-zallat a'naquhum,' what remains would still convey its meaning, because when men are humbled, their necks are humbled, and when their necks are humbled, they are humbled."

Commentary of al-Baghawi (*Ma'alim al-Tanzil*) on surah 26, verses 5–10:

﴿Never does there come to them any reminder from the Most Merciful﴾: an admonition and a reminder. ﴿Renewed﴾: meaning its revelation is renewed, so it is "renewed" in its sending down. Al-Kalbi said: Whenever some part of the Qur'an was revealed after another part, it was more recent than the first. ﴿But they turned away from it﴾: meaning from believing in it.

﴿So they have indeed denied, and there will come to them﴾: meaning, there will certainly come to them ﴿the news﴾: reports and consequences ﴿of what they used to mock.﴾ ﴿Have they not looked at the earth, how many noble kinds of every pair We have caused to grow therein?﴾: kind and sort. ﴿Noble﴾: good plants, of those that people and livestock eat. It is said: a palm tree is "noble" when its fruit is good, and a she-camel is "noble" when her milk is abundant. Al-Sha'bi said: People are from the plants of the earth; whoever enters Paradise is noble, and whoever enters the Fire is base. [[Narrated by al-Firyabi, 'Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim. Al-Durr al-Manthur: 6/289.]] ﴿Indeed in that﴾: what I have mentioned ﴿is surely a sign﴾: an indication of My existence, My oneness, and the perfection of My power. ﴿But most of them are not believers﴾: not affirming. That is, My knowledge had already preceded regarding them that most of them would not believe. Sibawayh said: "kana" here is a *silah* (a redundant, filler element of the sentence with no independent meaning), its sense being: "and most of them are not believers."

﴿And indeed your Lord is the Mighty﴾: the Mighty in exacting vengeance from His enemies, ﴿the Merciful﴾: full of mercy toward His friends.

His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿And when your Lord called Moses﴾: and remember, O Muhammad, when your Lord called Moses, when he saw the tree and the fire, ﴿saying: Go to the wrongdoing people﴾: meaning those who wronged themselves through disbelief and disobedience, and who wronged the Children of Israel by enslaving them and inflicting on them the worst torment.

**Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on Surah 26, verses 11–17:**

﴿The people of Pharaoh. Will they not be wary?﴾ That is, will they not guard themselves against the punishment of God by obeying Him?

﴿He said﴾ meaning Moses, ﴿"My Lord, I fear that they will deny me. And my breast will be constricted, and my tongue will not be loosed."﴾ The constriction of his breast is from their denial of me. ﴿And my tongue will not be loosed.﴾ He said: this refers to the knot that was on his tongue. Ya'qub (Ya'qub, a reader of the Qur'an) recited *wa-yadiqa* and *wa-la yanṭaliqa* with a fatha on both qafs, meaning *wa-an yadiqa* (and that it constrict). The majority (al-'Amma, the common reading) recited both with a damma, as a response to his saying *"innī akhāfu"* (I fear). ﴿So send to Harun﴾ that he may assist me and support me in conveying the message.

﴿And they have a charge against me﴾ that is, a claim of a crime, which is his killing of the Coptic man. ﴿So I fear that they will kill me﴾ that is, they will kill me for it.

﴿He said﴾ God, Exalted, said: ﴿"No!"﴾ that is, they will not kill you. ﴿So go, both of you, with Our signs. Indeed, We are with you, listening.﴾ Hearing what they say. He mentioned *"maʿakum"* (with you) in the plural, though there were two of them, treating them as a group. It was also said: He meant *maʿakumā* (with you two), and with the Children of Israel, We hear what Pharaoh answers you.

﴿So come to Pharaoh and say: "Indeed, we are a messenger of the Lord of the worlds."﴾ He did not say *"rasūlā"* (two messengers) because he meant the message, that is: I am one bearing the message of the Lord of the worlds, just as Kuthayyir said:

*"The slanderers have lied; I did not reveal to them any secret, nor did I send them as a messenger."* [[This verse is by Kuthayyir ʿAzza, and it was cited by al-Tabari (19/65), Abu ʿUbayda (2/84), and Ibn Manzur in Lisan al-ʿArab, root "r-s-l".]]

That is, with the message. Abu ʿUbayda said: it is permissible for *rasūl* to be used with the meaning of the dual and the plural. The Arabs say: "This is my messenger and my agent," and "These two are my messenger and my agent," and "These are my messengers and my agents," as God, Exalted, said: ﴿And they are your enemy﴾ [al-Kahf: 50]. It was also said: its meaning is that each one of us is a messenger of the Lord of the worlds. [[See: al-Bahr al-Muhit, 7/8.]]

﴿That you send﴾ that is, that you send, ﴿with us the Children of Israel﴾ to Palestine, and do not enslave them. Pharaoh had enslaved them for four hundred years, and at that time they numbered six hundred and thirty thousand. Moses set out for Egypt, while Harun was there, and he informed him of this.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 26, verses 21–22:

﴿So I fled from you when I feared you﴾ to Madyan, ﴿then my Lord granted me wisdom﴾, meaning prophethood. Muqatil said: it means knowledge and understanding. ﴿And made me one of the messengers﴾. ﴿And is this a favour you claim over me, that you enslaved the Children of Israel?﴾

Scholars differed in its interpretation. Some took it as an affirmation (iqrar) and others as a denial (inkar). Whoever said it is an affirmation said: Musa counted it as a favour from Pharaoh to him, since he raised him and did not kill him as he killed the other boys of the Children of Israel, and did not enslave him as he enslaved the Children of Israel. Its meaning (majazuhu) is: "Yes, and this is a favour upon me, that you enslaved the Children of Israel, and left me so that you did not enslave me."

Whoever said it is a denial said that his words "and is this a favour" are in the form of a question (istifham), meaning: "Or is this a favour?" The interrogative alif has been dropped, as in His words: ﴿Are they then the ones who will abide forever?﴾ [al-Anbiya': 34]. The poet said:

Are you leaving the tribe, or hastening away? ... And what harm would it do you to wait?

That is: "Are you leaving the tribe?" 'Umar ibn Abd Allah ibn Abi Rabi'a said:

I have not forgotten the day of departure, when she was mounted, ... and her eye was drowned in her tears.

And her saying, while the riding-camels stood still, ... "You leave me like this and go away?"

That is: "Will you leave me?" He says: "You claim a favour over me in that you raised me, and you forget your crime against the Children of Israel through enslavement and vile treatment?" Or he means: "How can you claim a favour over me by raising me when you have enslaved my people? Whoever has his people humiliated is himself humiliated, so your enslaving of the Children of Israel has nullified your kindness to me." It was also said that its meaning is: "You claim a favour over me by raising me."

As for His words ﴿that you enslaved the Children of Israel﴾, that is: by your enslaving the Children of Israel and killing their sons, I was delivered to you until you raised me and took charge of me. Had you not enslaved and killed them, I would have had among my own family someone to raise me, and they would not have cast me into the river. So what favour is it of yours upon me?

His words ﴿ʿabbadta﴾ mean: you took them as slaves. It is said: ʿabbadtu fulanan, and aʿbadtuhu, and taʿabbadtuhu, and istaʿbadtuhu, meaning: I took him as a slave.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 26, verses 23–30:

﴿Pharaoh said, "And what is the Lord of the worlds?"﴾ He means: "What is the Lord of the worlds, whom you claim you were sent to me as a messenger of?" He asks him to describe his God who sent him, using "mā" (what), which is a question about the kind or essence of a thing, and Allah is exalted above being a kind (of thing). So Musa (peace be upon him) answered him by mentioning His acts, which he (Pharaoh) is unable to produce the like of.

﴿He said, "Lord of the heavens and the earth and whatever is between them, if you are certain."﴾ That is, He is their Creator. The scholars of meanings (ahl al-ma'ani) said: meaning, just as you are certain of these things which you witness, then be certain that the God of creation is Allah, Mighty and Majestic. When Musa said this, Pharaoh was bewildered in his answer to Musa.

﴿He said to those around him﴾ from among the nobles of his people. Ibn Abbas said: they were five hundred men wearing bracelets. Pharaoh said to them, in amazement at Musa's words: ﴿"Do you not listen?"﴾ This is because they used to believe that their gods were their kings. So Musa increased his explanation.

﴿He said, "Your Lord and the Lord of your forefathers, the earliest ones."﴾ ﴿He said﴾ — i.e., Pharaoh: ﴿"Indeed, your messenger who has been sent to you is surely mad."﴾ He speaks words we do not understand and whose soundness we do not know. They held that whoever does not believe what they believe is not rational. So Musa increased his explanation: ﴿He said, "Lord of the east and the west and whatever is between them, if you have sense."﴾ ﴿He said﴾ — Pharaoh, when the proof had overwhelmed him and he was cut off from an answer — out of arrogance toward the truth: ﴿"If you take a god other than me, I will surely make you among the imprisoned."﴾ That is, among those confined. Al-Kalbi said: his imprisonment was worse than killing, for he would seize a man and cast him alone in a place by himself, where he would hear and see nothing, and he would be sent down into the earth.

﴿He said﴾ to him, Musa, when he threatened him with prison: ﴿"Even if I bring you something clear?"﴾ That is: "even if I bring you," ﴿"something clear"﴾ — a manifest sign. The meaning of the verse: "Will you do that even if I bring you a clear proof?" Musa said this because it is among human dispositions to be moved toward fairness and to accept the truth after it has been made clear.

﴿He said, "Lord of the heavens and the earth and whatever is between them, if you are certain."﴾ That is, He is their Creator. The scholars of meanings (ahl al-ma'ani) said: meaning, just as you are certain of these things which you witness, then be certain that the God of creation is Allah, Mighty and Majestic. When Musa said this, Pharaoh was bewildered in his answer to Musa.

﴿He said to those around him﴾ from among the nobles of his people. Ibn Abbas said: they were five hundred men wearing bracelets. Pharaoh said to them, in amazement at Musa's words: ﴿"Do you not listen?"﴾ This is because they used to believe that their gods were their kings. So Musa increased his explanation.

﴿He said, "Your Lord and the Lord of your forefathers, the earliest ones."﴾ ﴿He said﴾ — i.e., Pharaoh: ﴿"Indeed, your messenger who has been sent to you is surely mad."﴾ He speaks words we do not understand and whose soundness we do not know. They held that whoever does not believe what they believe is not rational. So Musa increased his explanation: ﴿He said, "Lord of the east and the west and whatever is between them, if you have sense."﴾ ﴿He said﴾ — Pharaoh, when the proof had overwhelmed him and he was cut off from an answer — out of arrogance toward the truth: ﴿"If you take a god other than me, I will surely make you among the imprisoned."﴾ That is, among those confined. Al-Kalbi said: his imprisonment was worse than killing, for he would seize a man and cast him alone in a place by himself, where he would hear and see nothing, and he would be sent down into the earth.

﴿He said﴾ to him, Musa, when he threatened him with prison: ﴿"Even if I bring you something clear?"﴾ That is: "even if I bring you," ﴿"something clear"﴾ — a manifest sign. The meaning of the verse: "Will you do that even if I bring you a clear proof?" Musa said this because it is among human dispositions to be moved toward fairness and to accept the truth after it has been made clear.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (*Ma'alim al-Tanzil*) on Surah 26, verses 31–43:

﴿He said﴾ to him, Pharaoh, ﴿"Then bring it, if you are of the truthful."﴾ For we will not imprison you then. ﴿So he threw down his staff, and behold, it was a clearly visible serpent.﴾ Pharaoh said: "Has it changed anything?"

﴿And he drew out﴾ Moses ﴿his hand, and behold, it was white to the onlookers.﴾ ﴿Pharaoh said to the chiefs around him, "Indeed, this is a skilled magician. He wants to drive you out of your land with his magic, so what do you advise?"﴾ ﴿They said, "Put him off and his brother, and send couriers into the cities to gather"﴾ ﴿and bring you every skilled magician.﴾

﴿So the magicians were gathered for the appointed time of a known day.﴾ That was the Day of the Festival. It is related from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: That day coincided with a Saturday, at the beginning of the year, and it was the day of Nayruz (the Persian New Year festival).

﴿And it was said to the people, "Will you assemble?"﴾ So that you may look at what the two parties do, and to whom the victory will go. ﴿"Perhaps we will follow the magicians, if they are the victors."﴾ That is, so that we may follow Moses. It was also said that they said this in mockery, and by "the magicians" they meant Moses, Aaron and their people.

﴿So when the magicians came, they said to Pharaoh, "Will there truly be a reward for us if we are the victors?"﴾

﴿He said, "Yes, and you will then indeed be among those brought near."﴾

﴿Moses said to them, "Throw down what you are going to throw."﴾

The meaning is: they angered us by opposing our religion, killing our sons, taking away our wealth which they had borrowed, and leaving our land without our permission.

﴿And indeed we are a wary, alert multitude﴾. The people of Hijaz and Basra read ﴿ḥadhirūn﴾ and ﴿fārihīn﴾ without the alif, while the others read ﴿ḥāwidhirūn﴾ and ﴿fārihīn﴾ with the alif in both. Commentary of al-Baghawi (*Ma'alim al-Tanzil*) on Surah 26, verses 59–63:

﴿Thus﴾, as We have described, ﴿and We made the Children of Israel inherit it﴾ after their destruction. This was because God Most High returned the Children of Israel to Egypt after He had drowned Pharaoh and his people, and He gave them all the wealth and dwellings that had belonged to Pharaoh and his people.

﴿So they pursued them at sunrise﴾, meaning they overtook them at the time of the sun's rising (*ishraq*), which is its brightening. That is, Pharaoh's people caught up with Moses and his companions at the time of the sunrise.

﴿And when the two groups came in sight of each other﴾, meaning they came face to face, so that each party saw the other. Hamzah read the *ra'* in *tara'a* with a kasra, while the others read it with a fatha.

﴿The companions of Moses said, "We are surely overtaken﴾, meaning: Pharaoh's people will overtake us, and we have no power against them.

﴿He said﴾, Moses, trusting in God's promise to him: ﴿"No! Surely my Lord is with me; He will guide me"﴾, meaning He will show me the way of deliverance.

﴿Then We revealed to Moses, "Strike the sea with your staff." So it parted﴾, meaning he struck it and it split open (*fa-infalaqa*), ﴿and every part was like a great mountain﴾, meaning like a huge mountain. Ibn Jurayj and others said [[Reported by al-Tabari: 19/80.]]: When Moses reached the sea, the wind blew and the sea was hurling waves like mountains. Yusha' said, "O speaker with God, where have you been commanded to go? Pharaoh has overtaken us and the sea is before us." Moses said, "Here." So Yusha' plunged into the water and crossed the sea, with the water not covering the hooves of his mount. The one who was hiding his faith said, "O speaker with God, where have you been commanded?" He said, "Here." So he restrained his horse with its bridle until the foam flew from its jaws. Then the sea engulfed him and he plunged into the water. The people then tried to do the same, but they could not. Moses did not know what to do, so God revealed to him, "Strike the sea with your staff." He struck it, and it split open, and there was the rider standing on his horse, with neither its saddle nor its saddle-cloth wet.

﴿وَأَزْلَفْنَا﴾ means "and We brought near," i.e., We drew close, ﴿ثَمَّ الْآخَرِينَ﴾ "there, the others," meaning the people of Pharaoh. It means that We brought them forward to the sea and brought them near to destruction. Abu Ubayda said: "*wa-azlafna*" means "We gathered," and from it comes *laylat al-Muzdalifa* (the Night of Muzdalifa), i.e., the night of gathering. In the narrative, Jibril (Gabriel) was between the Children of Israel and the people of Pharaoh. He was driving the Children of Israel, and they said, "We have never seen a better driver than this man," and he was restraining the people of Pharaoh, and they said, "We have never seen a better restrainer than this man." [[Narrated by Ibn Abd al-Hakam and Abd ibn Humayd from Mujahid. See: al-Durr al-Manthur: 6/304.]]

﴿وَأَنْجَيْنَا مُوسَى وَمَنْ مَعَهُ أَجْمَعِينَ﴾ "And We saved Musa and all those with him."

﴿ثُمَّ أَغْرَقْنَا الْآخَرِينَ﴾ "Then We drowned the others," meaning Pharaoh and his people. Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: The sea had been calm before that, but when Musa struck it with his staff, it began to churn, rising and falling.

﴿إِنَّ فِي ذَلِكَ لَآيَةً وَمَا كَانَ أَكْثَرُهُمْ مُؤْمِنِينَ﴾ "Indeed, in that is a sign, but most of them were not believers," i.e., most of the people of Egypt. It is said that none of the people of Egypt believed except Asiya, the wife of Pharaoh, and Hizbil the believer, and Maryam daughter of Naqusa, who guided them to the bones of Yusuf, peace be upon him.

﴿وَإِنَّ رَبَّكَ لَهُوَ الْعَزِيزُ الرَّحِيمُ﴾ "And indeed your Lord is the Almighty, the Most Merciful." Al-'Aziz (the Almighty) in exacting vengeance upon His enemies, and al-Rahim (the Most Merciful) toward the believers when He saved them. ﴿وَإِنَّ رَبَّكَ لَهُوَ الْعَزِيزُ الرَّحِيمُ﴾ "And indeed your Lord is the Almighty, the Most Merciful." Al-'Aziz (the Almighty) in exacting vengeance upon His enemies, and al-Rahim (the Most Merciful) toward the believers when He saved them. His saying: ﴿وَاتْلُ عَلَيْهِمْ نَبَأَ إِبْرَاهِيمَ﴾ "And recite to them the news of Ibrahim." His saying: ﴿إِذْ قَالَ لِأَبِيهِ وَقَوْمِهِ مَا تَعْبُدُونَ﴾ "When he said to his father and his people, 'What do you worship?'" That is, "What is it that you worship?"

﴿قَالُوا نَعْبُدُ أَصْنَامًا فَنَظَلُّ لَهَا عَاكِفِينَ﴾ "They said, 'We worship idols, and we remain devoted to them.'" That is, we persist in worshipping them. Some scholars said: He said *fa-nazallu* only because they used to worship them during the day and not at night; it is said *zalla yaf'alu kadhā* when someone does such a thing during the daytime.

﴿قَالَ هَلْ يَسْمَعُونَكُمْ﴾ "He said, 'Do they hear you'" — that is, do they hear your supplication — ﴿إِذْ تَدْعُونَ﴾ "when you call upon them?" Ibn Abbas said: "They hear you."

﴿أَوْ يَنْفَعُونَكُمْ﴾ "Or do they benefit you?" It was said: with provision. ﴿أَوْ يَضُرُّونَ﴾ "Or do they harm you?" if you abandon their worship.

**Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on Surah 26, verses 74–79:**

﴿They said: "Rather, we found our fathers doing thus."﴾ Its meaning: these idols do not hear any speech, do not bring any benefit, and do not repel any harm, but we followed our fathers. In it is the refutation of *taqlid* (blind imitation) in religion.

﴿He said: "Have you considered what you have been worshipping, you and your forefathers, the ancient ones?"﴾ The ancient ones, the earlier ones.

﴿"For they are an enemy to me."﴾ That is: they are enemies to me. He used the singular *ʿaduwwun* (enemy) to mean that every object of worship you have is an enemy to me. If it is asked: how did he describe the idols as enemies when they are inanimate objects? It is said: the meaning is that they would be an enemy to me if I worshipped them on the Day of Resurrection, [[Al-Nahhas considered this one of the most correct explanations of the meaning of the verse. Ma'ani al-Qur'an: 5/87; al-Tabari: 19/84.]] as He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿They will deny their worship of them and will become opponents to them﴾ [Maryam: 82]. Al-Farra' [[Ma'ani al-Qur'an by al-Farra': 2/281; Abu Hayyan rejected it in al-Bahr: 7/24.]] said it is of the inverted type (*al-maqlub*, a figure of speech in which the terms are reversed), and he intended: "Indeed I am an enemy to them, because whoever you oppose has opposed you." It was also said: "For they are an enemy to me" means: I do not take them as allies, and I do not seek benefit from them, just as one does not take an enemy as an ally nor seek benefit from him.

His saying: ﴿"Except the Lord of the worlds"﴾ Scholars differed regarding this exception. It was said: it is an exception of disjunction (*istithna' munqati'*, an exception where the excluded item is not of the same category as what precedes), as if he said: "They are an enemy to me, but the Lord of the worlds is my Protector." [[This is the view of most grammarians. See: al-Bahr al-Muhit: 7/24; Ma'ani al-Qur'an by al-Nahhas: 5/86; Zad al-Masir: 6/128.]] It was also said: they used to worship the idols alongside God, so Abraham said: "Everything you worship is my enemy, except the Lord of the worlds." [[Said by Ibn Zayd. Zad al-Masir: 6/128.]] It was also said: they are not an object of worship for me, except the Lord of the worlds, for I worship Him. Al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl said: its meaning is "except for one who worships the Lord of the worlds." Then he described his object of worship, saying: ﴿"Who created me, and it is He who guides me"﴾ That is: He guides me to the path of salvation.

﴿"And who feeds me and gives me drink"﴾ That is: He provides for me and nourishes me with food and drink; so He is my Provider, and my provision comes from Him.

إِذَا مَرِضْتُ: أَضَافَ الْمَرَضَ إِلَى نَفْسِهِ، وَإِنْ كَانَ الْمَرَضُ وَالشِّفَاءُ كُلُّهُ مِنَ اللَّهِ، اسْتِعْمَالًا لِحُسْنِ الْأَدَبِ، كَمَا قَالَ الْخَضِرُ: "فَأَرَدْتُ أَنْ أَعِيبَهَا" [الكهف: ٧٩]، وَقَالَ: "فَأَرَادَ رَبُّكَ أَنْ يَبْلُغَا أَشُدَّهُمَا" [الكهف: ٨٢].

﴿فَهُوَ يَشْفِينِ﴾ أَيْ: يُبْرِئُنِي مِنَ الْمَرَضِ.

﴿وَالَّذِي يُمِيتُنِي ثُمَّ يُحْيِينِ﴾ أَدْخَلَ "ثُمَّ" هَاهُنَا لِلتَّرَاخِي، أَيْ: يُمِيتُنِي فِي الدُّنْيَا وَيُحْيِينِي فِي الْآخِرَةِ.

﴿وَالَّذِي أَطْمَعُ﴾ أَيْ: أَرْجُو، ﴿أَنْ يَغْفِرَ لِي خَطِيئَتِي يَوْمَ الدِّينِ﴾ أَيْ: خَطَايَايَ يَوْمَ الْحِسَابِ. قَالَ مُجَاهِدٌ: هِيَ قَوْلُهُ: "إِنِّي سَقِيمٌ"، وَقَوْلُهُ: ﴿بَلْ فَعَلَهُ كَبِيرُهُمْ هَذَا﴾، وَقَوْلُهُ لِسَارَّةَ: "هَذِهِ أُخْتِي"، وَزَادَ الْحَسَنُ: وَقَوْلُهُ لِلْكَوَاكِبِ: "هَذَا رَبِّي".

وَأَخْبَرَنَا إِسْمَاعِيلُ بْنُ عَبْدِ الْقَاهِرِ، أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ الْغَافِرِ بْنُ مُحَمَّدٍ الْفَارِسِيُّ، أَخْبَرَنَا مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ عِيسَى الْجُلُودِيُّ، أَخْبَرَنَا إِبْرَاهِيمُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ سُفْيَانَ، حَدَّثَنَا مُسْلِمُ بْنُ الْحَجَّاجِ، حَدَّثَنَا أَبُو بَكْرِ بْنُ أَبِي شَيْبَةَ، حَدَّثَنَا حَفْصُ بْنُ غِيَاثٍ، عَنْ دَاوُدَ، عَنِ الشَّعْبِيِّ، عَنْ مَسْرُوقٍ، عَنْ عَائِشَةَ قَالَتْ: قُلْتُ: يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ، ابْنُ جُدْعَانَ كَانَ فِي الْجَاهِلِيَّةِ يَصِلُ الرَّحِمَ وَيُطْعِمُ الْمَسَاكِينَ، فَهَلْ ذَاكَ نَافِعُهُ؟ قَالَ: "لَا يَنْفَعُهُ، إِنَّهُ لَمْ يَقُلْ يَوْمًا: رَبِّ اغْفِرْ لِي خَطِيئَتِي يَوْمَ الدِّينِ" [[أخرجه مسلم في الإيمان، باب الدليل على أن من مات على الكفر لا ينفعه عمل، برقم (٢١٤): ١ / ١٩٦.]]

وَهَذَا كُلُّهُ احْتِجَاجٌ مِنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَلَى قَوْمِهِ، وَإِخْبَارٌ أَنَّهُ لَا يَصْلُحُ لِلْإِلَهِيَّةِ مَنْ لَا يَفْعَلُ هَذِهِ الْأَفْعَالَ.

﴿رَبِّ هَبْ لِي حُكْمًا﴾ قَالَ ابْنُ عَبَّاسٍ: مَعْرِفَةُ حُدُودِ اللَّهِ وَأَحْكَامِهِ. وَقَالَ مُقَاتِلٌ: الْفَهْمُ وَالْعِلْمُ. وَقَالَ الْكَلْبِيُّ: النُّبُوَّةُ [[اعتمده الطبري ولم يذكر غيره، وهو مروي أيضًا عن ابن عباس، وانظر الأقوال في: زاد المسير: ٦ / ١٣٠.]].

﴿وَأَلْحِقْنِي بِالصَّالِحِينَ﴾ بِمَنْ قَبْلِي مِنَ النَّبِيِّينَ فِي الْمَنْزِلَةِ وَالدَّرَجَةِ.

**Al-Baghawi, *Ma'alim al-Tanzil* (The Landmarks of Revelation), on Surah 26, verses 86–96:**

﴿And forgive my father, for indeed he was among the misguided.﴾ He said this before it became clear to him that he was an enemy of Allah, as was mentioned earlier in Surah al-Tawbah.

﴿And do not disgrace me﴾ means do not expose me to shame, ﴿on the Day they are resurrected,﴾ ﴿the Day when neither wealth nor children will benefit, except one who comes to Allah with a sound heart.﴾ That is, free from shirk (associating partners with Allah) and doubt. [[See: al-Tabari, 19/87; al-Nahhas, *Ma'ani al-Qur'an*, 5/88.]] As for sins, no one is free from them. This is the view of most exegetes. Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib said: the sound heart is the healthy heart, which is the heart of the believer, because the heart of the disbeliever and the hypocrite is diseased. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿In their hearts is a disease﴾ [al-Baqarah: 10]. Ibn Uthman al-Naysaburi said: it is the heart that is free from innovation and at peace with the Sunnah. [[All of this is quoted by Ibn Kathir in his *Tafsir*, 3/341. See also Zad al-Masir, 6/130.]]

﴿And Paradise will be brought near﴾ means brought close, ﴿to the righteous,﴾ ﴿and Hellfire will be made apparent﴾ means made visible, ﴿to the misguided,﴾ meaning the disbelievers.

﴿And it will be said to them﴾ on the Day of Resurrection, ﴿Where are those you used to worship﴾ ﴿besides Allah? Can they help you﴾ meaning protect you ﴿from punishment, or can they defend themselves?﴾

﴿So they will be overturned into it﴾. Ibn Abbas said: they will be gathered together. Mujahid said: they will be hurled down. Muqatil said: they will be thrown. Al-Zajjaj said: some of them will be cast upon others. Al-Qutaybi said: they will be thrown onto their faces.

﴿They and the misguided﴾ meaning the devils, as said by Qatada and Muqatil. Al-Kalbi said: the disbelieving jinn.

﴿And the armies of Iblis, all of them.﴾ They are his followers and those among the jinn and humans who obeyed him. It is also said: his offspring.

﴿They will say﴾ meaning the misguided will say to the devils and the deities that were worshipped, ﴿while they dispute among themselves therein,﴾ with the deities that were worshipped, and some of them argue with others.

**Surah 26, verses 97–105**

﴿By God, we were truly in clear error,﴾.

﴿When we made you equal﴾: we held you as equal, ﴿to the Lord of the worlds﴾, so that we worshipped you.

﴿And none led us astray﴾: that is, none invited us to error, ﴿except the criminals﴾. Muqatil said: they meant the devils (shayatin). Al-Kalbi said: except our forefathers whom we followed. Abu al-'Aliyah and 'Ikrimah said: they meant Iblis and the first son of Adam, who was Qabil, because he was the first to institute killing and various kinds of sin.

﴿So we have no intercessors﴾: that is, anyone from among the angels, prophets and believers who would intercede for us.

﴿Nor a close friend﴾: that is, a near one who would intercede for us. The disbelievers say this when the angels, prophets and believers are interceding. The friend (sadiq) is one who is sincere in affection, on the condition of religion. Abu Sa'id al-Shurayhi informed us: Abu Ishaq al-Tha'labi informed us: al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn Fanjawayh informed me: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn al-Yaqtini narrated to us: Ahmad ibn 'Abd Allah Yazid al-'Uqayli informed us: Safwan ibn Salih narrated to us: al-Walid ibn Muslim narrated to us: from one who heard Abu al-Zubayr say: "I testify that I heard Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah say: I heard the Messenger of God (ﷺ) say: 'A man will say in Paradise, "What has become of my friend so-and-so?" while his friend is in Hellfire. God, exalted is He, will say: "Bring out his friend to Paradise." Then the one who remains will say: "So we have no intercessors, nor a close friend."'" [Al-Qurtubi mentioned it in his tafsir (13/118), but none of the authors of the Six Books or others narrated it. The author transmitted it with its chain through al-Tha'labi, and in it there is an unidentified narrator, the one who heard Abu al-Zubayr.] Al-Hasan said: "Acquire many believing friends, for they have intercession on the Day of Resurrection."

﴿So if only we had a return﴾: that is, a return to the world, ﴿then we would be among the believers﴾.

﴿Indeed in that is a sign, yet most of them were not believers﴾. ﴿And indeed your Lord, He is the Mighty, the Merciful﴾. Al-'Aziz is the one who cannot be overcome. God is Mighty, and in describing His might He is merciful.

The saying of the Exalted, Majestic One: ﴿The people of Noah denied the messengers﴾. It was said to al-Hasan al-Basri: "O Abu Sa'id, what do you say about His words: ﴿The people of Noah denied the messengers﴾, ﴿'Ad denied the messengers﴾, and ﴿Thamud denied the messengers﴾, when only one messenger was sent to each of them?" He said: "The other came with what the first came with. So when they denied one, they denied all the messengers."

﴿When their brother said to them﴾ (i.e., a brother in lineage, not in religion).

﴿Noah, will you not fear God?﴾ ﴿Indeed I am a trustworthy messenger to you﴾ (trusted with the revelation).

﴿So fear God﴾ by obeying Him and worshipping Him, ﴿and obey me﴾ in what I command you concerning faith and monotheism.

﴿And I do not ask you for any wage for it; my wage is only from﴾ my Lord, ﴿the Lord of the worlds﴾. ﴿So fear God and obey me﴾.

﴿They said, "Shall we believe you while the lowest-born follow you?"﴾ Ya'qub (Yaʿqub) recited it as "وَأَتْبَاعُكَ الْأَرْذَلُونَ" (wa-atbāʿuka al-arḏalūn, "and your followers are the lowest"), a variant reading (qirāʾah). Al-Arḏalūn means "the lowest," that is, "the base people." It is narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās that he said: they were the goldsmiths (al-ṣāghah). ʿIkrimah said: they were the weavers (al-ḥākah) and the cobblers (al-asākifah).

﴿He said﴾ (Noah), ﴿"And I have no knowledge of what they used to do"﴾, meaning: I do not know their deeds and crafts. There is no burden on me for the lowliness of their trades and conditions. I was only commanded to call them to God, and I am responsible only for their outward state.

﴿Their reckoning is only﴾ what it is, ﴿but with my Lord, if you could perceive﴾, if you knew this, you would not have reproached them for their crafts. Al-Zajjaj said: crafts do not harm one's religion. It was also said: the meaning is, "I did not know that God would guide them and misguide you, grant them success and forsake you."

﴿And I am not one to drive away the believers. I am only a plain warner﴾.

﴿They said, "If you do not desist, O Noah, from what you are saying, you will surely be among those stoned"﴾. Muqatil and al-Kalbi said: among those killed by stones. Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: among those reviled.

His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿The people of ʿĀd denied the messengers.﴾ ﴿When their brother Hud said to them,﴾ meaning in lineage, not in religion, ﴿"Will you not fear Allah?"﴾ ﴿Indeed I am to you a trustworthy messenger,﴾ in conveying the message. Al-Kalbi said: "Trustworthy among you before the prophethood, so how would you accuse me today?"

﴿So fear Allah and obey me.﴾ ﴿And I do not ask you for any wage for it; my wage is only from the Lord of the worlds.﴾ ﴿Do you build on every high place [rīʿ] a monument?﴾ Al-Waliby related from Ibn ʿAbbas: that is, on every noble place. Al-Ḍaḥḥāk, Muqatil and al-Kalbi said: on every road; this is also the report of al-ʿAwfi from Ibn ʿAbbas. From Mujahid: it is the path between two mountains. Also from him: it is the lookout.

﴿A sign﴾ meaning a landmark, ﴿that you mock﴾ those who pass by on the road. The meaning is that they used to build elevated places to look down on passersby and travelers, so that they would ridicule and mock them. From Saʿid ibn Jubayr and Mujahid: this refers to dovecotes; Hud denounced them for making these, based on His saying "you mock" (taʿbathūna), meaning you play, and they used to play with doves. Abu ʿUbayda said: the rīʿ is an elevated place.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 26, verse 129–137:

﴿And you take for yourselves ma–ani'* (fortresses/edifices)﴾. Ibn ʿAbbas said: buildings. Mujahid said: lofty palaces. It is related from al-Kalbi that they were fortresses. Qatadah said: water reservoirs, meaning cisterns, the singular of which is maṣna‘ah.

[[al-Tabari said (19/95–96): "The correct statement on this matter is that it should be said: al-maṣani' is the plural of maṣna‘ah, and the Arabs call every building a maṣna‘ah. It is possible that this building was palaces and lofty fortresses, and it is possible that it was water intakes. There is no report that settles the matter as to which of these it was, nor is it something that can be known by reason. So the correct approach is to say about it what Allah said: that they used to take maṣani'."]]

﴿So that you may live forever﴾, that is, as if you would remain in them forever. The meaning is that they used to build the maṣani' as if they would never die.

﴿And when you seize [others]﴾: you take them and assault them, ﴿seize as tyrants﴾: killing by the sword and striking with the whip. The jabbar (tyrant) is one who kills and strikes in anger.

﴿So fear Allah and obey me﴾.

﴿And fear the One who has aided you with what you know﴾: that is, He has given you of the good things that you know. Then he mentioned what He had given them, saying: ﴿He has aided you with cattle and children﴾ ﴿and gardens and springs﴾, that is, orchards and rivers.

﴿Indeed, I fear for you﴾: Ibn ʿAbbas said: if you disobey me, ﴿the punishment of a tremendous day﴾.

﴿They said: it is all the same to us﴾, that is, equal in our view, ﴿whether you admonish or are not among the admonishers﴾. Waʿẓ (admonition) is speech that softens the heart by mentioning promise and threat. al-Kalbi said: whether you forbid us or are not among those who forbid us.

**Al-Baghawi, *Ma'alim al-Tanzil*, on Surah 26, verses 138–148:**

﴿And we are not going to be punished.﴾ ﴿So they denied him, and We destroyed them. Indeed in that is a sign, but most of them were not believers.﴾ ﴿And indeed your Lord is the Mighty, the Merciful.﴾

His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿The Thamud denied the messengers. When their brother Salih said to them, "Will you not fear God? Indeed I am a trustworthy messenger to you. So fear God and obey me. And I do not ask you for any wage for it; my wage is only from the Lord of the worlds. Will you be left secure in what is here"﴾, meaning: in this world, ﴿secure﴾ from punishment.

﴿In gardens and springs and fields and palm trees, whose spathes (ṭalʿuhā)﴾, meaning their fruit, by which is meant the fruit that emerges from them, ﴿are delicate (haḍīm)﴾. Ibn ʿAbbas said: "Slender (laṭīf)." From this comes the expression *haḍīm al-kashh*, meaning a slender waist. ʿAṭiyya narrated from him: "Ripe and mature (yāniʿ naḍīj)." ʿIkrima said: "Soft (layyin)." Al-Hasan said: "Loose and pliant (rakhw)." Mujahid said: "Broken and crumbling when touched, because while it is still moist it is *haḍīm*, and when it dries it becomes *hashīm*." Al-Ḍaḥḥak and Muqatil said: "Some of it has ridden over other parts of it, until some of it crushed the rest," that is, broke it. The lexicographers said: "It is what is pressed together, one part against another, within its sheath before it appears." Al-Azhari said: "*Al-Haḍīm* is that in which some parts have entered into others because of ripeness and softness." It was also said: *haḍīm* means *hāḍim*, that which digests food. All of these meanings refer to its delicacy.

*[Footnote:]* These sayings are mentioned by al-Ṭabari (19/99–100), Ibn al-Jawzi (6/138) and al-Qurtubi (13/128), and there are other sayings regarding the verse. Al-Ṭabari said: "The most correct of the sayings on this matter is that it is said: *al-haḍīm* is that which is broken because of its softness and moisture. This derives from their saying: *haḍama fulān ḥaqqahu*, when he diminished it and encroached upon it. So *haḍm* in the spathe is the diminishing of it because of its moisture and softness, either by the touching of hands or by some of it riding over others. Its origin is a passive form (*mafʿūl*) that was changed to the form *faʿīl*."

*[Note in the edition: the bracketed text is absent from manuscript "B".]*

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 26, verse 149–155:

﴿And you hew out of the mountains houses, exulting in your skill.﴾ It is also read "fārihīn" (skilled, exulting). It was said: their meaning is one and the same [[This is the view taken by Abu 'Ubaydah in "Majaz al-Qur'an": 2 / 98.]]. It was also said: fārihīn means: skilled in hewing them, from the saying "fariha al-rajul farāhatan, fa-huwa fārih" (the man became skilled, so he is skilled). As for the one who reads "fārihīn," Ibn 'Abbas said: insolent and arrogant. 'Ikrimah said: luxurious. Mujahid said: greedy. Qatadah said: pleased with your handiwork. Al-Suddi said: tyrannical. Abu 'Ubaydah said: exultant. Al-Akhfash said: "farihīn" (joyful). The Arabs interchange the letter hā' and ḥā' such as "madahtuhu" and "madahtuhu" (I praised him). Al-Dahhak said: clever [[Al-Tabari, after presenting the sayings on the interpretation of the two readings, said (19 / 101): "The correct view is that they are two well-known readings, widely transmitted among the scholars of recitation, so whichever of them a reader recites is correct. The meaning of the reading (fārihīn) is: skilled in hewing them, choosing the places for hewing, clever, from al-farāha. The meaning of the reading (fārihīn) is: exultant, insolent; and it is permissible that the meaning of fāri and fārih be one..".]].

﴿So fear Allah and obey me, and do not obey the command of the extravagant,﴾ Ibn 'Abbas said: the polytheists. Muqatil said: they are the nine who hamstrung the she-camel.

﴿who cause corruption in the land﴾ by acts of disobedience, ﴿and do not reform﴾ they do not obey Allah in what He commanded them.

﴿They said: "You are only of those who are bewitched."﴾ Mujahid and Qatadah said: of those who are deceived (al-maskhurin al-makhdu'in), meaning: of those who have been bewitched again and again. Al-Kalbi related from Abu Salih from Ibn 'Abbas: meaning: of the created beings who are sustained by food and drink, it is said "sahharahu," meaning he sustained him with food and drink. The meaning is: you eat food and drink and are not an angel; rather, ﴿you are only a human like us, so bring a sign﴾ to confirm what you say, ﴿if you are of the truthful﴾ that you are the messenger of Allah to us.

﴿He said: "This is a she-camel; she has a share﴾ a portion and allotment of water, ﴿and for you is a share of a known day."﴾

It was said: their meaning is one and the same [[This is the view taken by Abu 'Ubaydah in "Majaz al-Qur'an": 2 / 98.]]. It was also said: fārihīn means: skilled in hewing them, from the saying "fariha al-rajul farāhatan, fa-huwa fārih" (the man became skilled, so he is skilled). As for the one who reads "fārihīn," Ibn 'Abbas said: insolent and arrogant. 'Ikrimah said: luxurious. Mujahid said: greedy. Qatadah said: pleased with your handiwork. Al-Suddi said: tyrannical. Abu 'Ubaydah said: exultant. Al-Akhfash said: "farihīn" (joyful). The Arabs interchange the letter hā' and ḥā' such as "madahtuhu" and "madahtuhu" (I praised him). Al-Dahhak said: clever [[Al-Tabari, after presenting the sayings on the interpretation of the two readings, said (19 / 101): "The correct view is that they are two well-known readings, widely transmitted among the scholars of recitation, so whichever of them a reader recites is correct. The meaning of the reading (fārihīn) is: skilled in hewing them, choosing the places for hewing, clever, from al-farāha. The meaning of the reading (fārihīn) is: exultant, insolent; and it is permissible that the meaning of fāri and fārih be one..".]].

﴿So fear Allah and obey me, and do not obey the command of the extravagant,﴾ Ibn 'Abbas said: the polytheists. Muqatil said: they are the nine who hamstrung the she-camel.

﴿who cause corruption in the land﴾ by acts of disobedience, ﴿and do not reform﴾ they do not obey Allah in what He commanded them.

﴿They said: "You are only of those who are bewitched."﴾ Mujahid and Qatadah said: of those who are deceived (al-maskhurin al-makhdu'in), meaning: of those who have been bewitched again and again. Al-Kalbi related from Abu Salih from Ibn 'Abbas: meaning: of the created beings who are sustained by food and drink, it is said "sahharahu," meaning he sustained him with food and drink. The meaning is: you eat food and drink and are not an angel; rather, ﴿you are only a human like us, so bring a sign﴾ to confirm what you say, ﴿if you are of the truthful﴾ that you are the messenger of Allah to us.

﴿He said: "This is a she-camel; she has a share﴾ a portion and allotment of water, ﴿and for you is a share of a known day."﴾

ثُمَّ دَمَّرْنَا الْآخَرِينَ — "Then We destroyed the others," meaning: We annihilated you.

﴿Then We destroyed the others.﴾ That is, "We destroyed them."

Correction of wording: The passage as given reads: ﴿ثُمَّ دَمَّرْنَا الْآخَرِينَ﴾ أَيْ: أَهْلَكْنَاكُمْ — here the translation follows directly below.

Let me give the translation as requested:

﴿Then We destroyed the others.﴾ That is: "We destroyed you."

﴿And We rained down upon them a rain, and evil was the rain of those who were warned.﴾ Wahb ibn Munabbih said: "It was sulphur and fire."

﴿Indeed in that is a sign, yet most of them were not believers.﴾ ﴿And indeed your Lord is the Mighty, the Merciful.﴾ Regarding His words, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿The companions of the Thicket denied the messengers.﴾ They are the people of Shu'ayb, peace be upon him. The Iraqi readers recited "al-Aykah" here and in Surah Sad with a hamza, a sukun on the lam, and a kasra on the ta'. The others recited "Laykah" with a fatha on the lam and the ta', without a hamza, treating it as the name of the town, and it is diptote (ghayr munsarif). They did not differ over Surah al-Hijr and Qaf, where both are with a hamza and a kasra. Al-Aykah is a thicket: a dense cluster of intertwined trees.

﴿When Shu'ayb said to them﴾ — he did not say "their brother," because he was not from the companions of the Thicket by lineage. When he mentioned Madyan, he said "their brother Shu'ayb," because he was from them. Allah Most High had sent him to his people, the people of Madyan, and to the companions of the Thicket.

﴿Will you not fear God?﴾ ﴿Indeed I am to you a trustworthy messenger. So fear God and obey me. And I do not ask you for any reward for it; my reward is only from the Lord of the worlds.﴾ The call of all these prophets, as Allah related of them, was in one single form, since they agreed on commanding taqwa, obedience, sincerity in worship, and abstaining from taking wages for the call and the conveyance of the message.

﴿Give full measure and do not be of those who cause loss,﴾ that is, those who diminish people's rights in measure and weight.

﴿And weigh with a true balance, and do not deprive people of their things, and do not commit corruption on the earth, causing mischief. And fear Him who created you and the former generations (al-jibillah).﴾ Al-jibillah: the creation, the earlier peoples, meaning the former nations. Al-jibillah means creation; it is said "jubila," meaning "khuliqa" (he was created).

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 26, verses 185–195:

﴿They said, "You are only one of those bewitched. You are but a human being like us, and we think you are indeed among the liars. So cause a piece of the sky to fall upon us, if you are of the truthful." He said, "My Lord knows best what you do."﴾ That is: of the diminishing of the measure and the weight. He will requite you for your deeds, and the punishment is not up to me; my duty is only to convey the message.

﴿So they denied him, and the punishment of the Day of the Shadow seized them.﴾ That was because a fierce heat seized them, so they would enter the caverns, but when they entered them they found them even hotter, so they came out. Then a cloud shaded them, and that is the "shadow" (al-Zullah). They gathered beneath it, and it rained fire upon them, so they were burned. We have mentioned this in Surat Hud.

﴿Indeed, it was the punishment of a tremendous day.﴾ ﴿Indeed in that is a sign, but most of them were not believers.﴾ ﴿And indeed your Lord is the Mighty, the Merciful.﴾ His saying, may He be exalted, ﴿And indeed it﴾ means the Qur'an.

﴿It is a revelation from the Lord of the worlds.﴾ ﴿The Trustworthy Spirit has brought it down.﴾ The people of the Hijaz, Abu 'Amr and Hafs read "nazala" with a light (unstressed) zāy, and "al-Ruhu al-Amin" with a ḍamma on the ḥā' and the nūn, meaning: Jibril (Gabriel) brought down the Qur'an. The others read it with a shadda on the zāy and a fatḥa on the ḥā' and the nūn, meaning: God sent down Jibril with it, in accordance with His saying, may He be exalted, "And indeed it is a revelation from the Lord of the worlds."

﴿Upon your heart﴾, O Muhammad, so that you may memorize it, ﴿that you may be one of the warners﴾, those who instil fear.

﴿In clear Arabic speech.﴾ [Ibn 'Abbas said: "In the speech of Quraysh, so that they may understand what is in it."] [[What is between the brackets is omitted from "A".]]

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 26, verse 196–200:

﴿And indeed it﴾ means: the mention of the sending down of the Qur'an. This is what most of the exegetes said. Muqatil said: it means the mention of Muhammad ﷺ and his description, ﴿is indeed in the scriptures of the former peoples﴾. ﴿Was it not a sign for them﴾ [Ibn 'Amir recited "takun" with a ta' and "ayatun" in the nominative, making the ayah the subject (ism) of the verb, with its predicate being ﴿that the scholars of the Children of Israel know it﴾. The others recited it with a ya' and "ayatan" in the accusative, making the ayah the predicate (khabar) of kana. The bracketed text is from manuscript "A".] The meaning: Was it not a sign for these deniers [in manuscript "B": the arrogant] that the learned men of the Children of Israel knew it, i.e., a sign and proof of the prophethood of Muhammad ﷺ? Because the scholars among the Children of Israel used to inform of the existence of his mention in their books, and they were: 'Abdullah ibn Salam and his companions [this is related from Mujahid; see al-Durr al-Manthur 6/322, al-Tabari 19/113]. Ibn 'Abbas said: The people of Makkah sent to the Jews, who were in Madinah, and asked them about Muhammad ﷺ. They said: Indeed this is the time of his coming, and we find his description and attributes in the Torah. So that was a sign of his truthfulness [see Zad al-Masir 6/145].

His saying the Exalted: ﴿that the scholars of the Children of Israel know it﴾, meaning: know Muhammad ﷺ. 'Ata' said: They were five: 'Abdullah ibn Salam, Ibn Yamin, Tha'labah, Asad, and Usayd [attributed by al-Suyuti in al-Durr (6/323) to 'Abd ibn Humayd and to Ibn Abi Hatim from Qatadah].

﴿And if We had sent it down﴾ meaning the Qur'an, ﴿upon some of the non-Arabs﴾ — the plural of a'jami, who is one who is not eloquent and does not speak Arabic well, even if he is Arab by lineage; and the 'ajami is one attributed to the non-Arabs, even if he is eloquent. The meaning of the verse: If We had sent it down upon a man who was not of Arabic tongue.

﴿And he recited it to them﴾ in other than the language of the Arabs, ﴿they would not have believed in it﴾, and they would have said: We do not understand your speech. Its parallel is the saying of the Mighty and Majestic: "And if We had made it a non-Arabic Qur'an, they would have said: Why are its verses not made clear?" [Fussilat: 44]. It was also said: its meaning is, if We had sent it down upon a man who was not from the Arabs, they would not have believed in it out of arrogance toward following him.

﴿Thus We let it enter﴾ — Ibn 'Abbas, al-Hasan and Mujahid said: We caused polytheism and denial to enter ﴿into the hearts of the criminals﴾.

**Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 26, verse 214:**

﴿And warn your nearest kinsmen﴾. Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated from Abd al-Ghaffar ibn al-Qasim, from al-Minhal ibn Amr, from Abd Allah ibn al-Harith ibn Nawfal ibn al-Harith ibn Abd al-Muttalib, from Abd Allah ibn Abbas, from Ali ibn Abi Talib. He said: When this verse was revealed to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), ﴿And warn your nearest kinsmen﴾, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) called me and said: "O Ali, Allah has commanded me to warn my nearest kinsmen, and I was distressed by this, for I knew that if I declared this matter to them, I would see from them what I dislike. So I remained silent about it. Then Jibril came to me and said: 'O Muhammad, if you do not do what you are commanded, your Lord will punish you. So prepare for us a sa' of food and put upon it a leg of sheep, and fill for us a large cup with milk. Then gather for me the sons of Abd al-Muttalib so that I may convey to them what I have been commanded.'" Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, said: So I did what the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had commanded me, then I invited them to him. They were on that day forty men, a man more or less, among them his paternal uncles Abu Talib, Hamza, al-Abbas, and Abu Lahab. When they had gathered around him, he called for the food that I had prepared, so I brought it. When I placed it down, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) took a morsel of meat, tore it with his teeth, then threw it into the sides of the dish, and said: "Take it in the name of Allah." The people ate until they no longer needed anything, and by Allah, one man among them would eat what I had prepared for all of them. Then he said: "Give the people to drink." So I brought them that cup, and they drank until they were all satisfied, and by Allah, one man among them would drink the like of it. When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) wished to speak to them, Abu Lahab forestalled him and said: "Your companion has bewitched you." So the people dispersed, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) did not speak to them. The next day he said: "O Ali, this man has forestalled me in what you heard from the people, and the people dispersed before I could speak to them. So prepare for us food like what you prepared, then gather them." I did so, then I gathered them, and he called for the food, so I brought it near. He did as he had done the day before, and they ate and drank. Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) spoke and said: "O sons of Abd al-Muttalib, I have come to you with the good of this world and the Hereafter. Allah, the Exalted, has commanded me to invite you to Him. So which of you will support me in this matter of mine, and will be my brother, my executor, and my successor among you?" The people all held back from it. I said, and I was the youngest of them in age: "I, O Prophet of Allah, will be your vizier in it." He said: So he took hold of my neck and said: "Indeed, this is my brother, my executor, and my successor among you, so listen to him and obey him." The people rose laughing, saying to Abu Talib: "He has commanded you to listen to Ali and obey him."

[[Narrated by Ibn Ishaq in al-Maghazi, and by al-Bayhaqi in "al-Dala'il" through his chain, from the narration of Ibn Abbas. It was also narrated by al-Bazzar and Abu Nu'aym in al-Dala'il through the route of Abbad ibn Abd Allah al-Asadi from Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him.

See: al-Kafi al-Shaf, p. (123). Refer also to the Tafsir of Ibn Kathir: 3 / 315-352, for he said: Abd al-Ghaffar ibn al-Qasim Abu Maryam alone narrated this context. He is abandoned (matruk), a liar, and a Shi'i. Ali ibn al-Madini and others accused him of fabricating hadith, and the Imams declared him weak, may Allah have mercy on them.]].

Al-Malihi, Abd al-Wahid ibn Ahmad, informed us; al-Nu'aymi, Ahmad ibn Abd Allah, informed us; Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us; Muhammad ibn Isma'il (al-Bukhari) narrated to us; Yusuf ibn Musa narrated to us; Abu Usama narrated to us; al-A'mash narrated to us; Amr ibn Murrah narrated to us, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, who said: When the verse was revealed, ﴿And warn your nearest kinsmen﴾, "and your kinsmen among them who are sincere (al-mukhlisin)", the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) went out until he climbed al-Safa, and shouted: "O, my companions!" They said: "Who is this?" So they gathered around him, and he said: "Tell me, if I informed you that cavalry were coming out from the side of this mountain, would you believe me?" They said: "We have never found you to lie." He said: "Then I am a warner to you before a severe punishment." Abu Lahab said: "Destruction to you! Did you gather us only for this?" Then he rose, and the following was revealed: ﴿Perish the hands of Abu Lahab, and perish he﴾. This is how al-A'mash recited it on that day.

[[Narrated by al-Bukhari in the tafsir of the surah "Tabbat", 8 / 737, and in funerals, and in the surahs al-Shu'ara' and Saba'. It was also narrated by Muslim in Iman, chapter on the saying of Allah, "And warn your nearest kinsmen", no. (208): 1 / 193-194. The author (al-Baghawi) also cites it in Sharh al-Sunna: 13 / 327.

Al-Nawawi said in Sharh Sahih Muslim (3 / 82), regarding the words "and your kinsmen among them who are sincere": "It is with a fatha on the lam (al-mukhlisin, as in the reading "al-mukhlisin"). The apparent meaning of this phrase is that the words 'and your kinsmen among them who are sincere' were a Qur'an that was revealed and then its recitation was abrogated (nuskha tilawatuhu, naskh al-tilawa, abrogation of recitation), and this addition does not occur in the narrations of al-Bukhari."

I say: Rather, it occurs in the narration of al-Bukhari in the previously mentioned place of the tafsir, 8 / 737, through the narration of Abu Usama from al-A'mash. Ibn Hajar said: "This addition was linked by al-Tabari through another route from Amr ibn Murrah, that he used to recite it in this way. Al-Qurtubi said: Perhaps this addition was a Qur'an whose recitation was abrogated. Then this is problematic, because the intent is the warning of the disbelievers, while 'al-mukhlisin' is a description of the believer?! The answer to this is that there is no impediment to conjoining the particular to the general. So His saying 'And warn your nearest kinsmen' is general, encompassing those among them who believed and those who did not, then the sincere kinsmen were conjoined to it to honour them and to emphasise them."

See: Fath al-Bari: 8 / 502; Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 13 / 143. As for the reading "wa-qad tabb" as in the narration, Ibn Hajar said regarding it in Fath al-Bari (8 / 503): "This reading is not among what the readers transmitted from al-A'mash. What appears is that he recited it as a narrator reporting it, not as a reader, and this is supported by his saying in this context 'on that day', which indicates that he did not persist in reciting it in this way. And what is preserved is that it is the reading of Ibn Mas'ud alone." Al-Badr al-Ayni said in Umdat al-Qari (20 / 7): "His saying 'and your kinsmen among them who are sincere' is either an explanation of his saying 'your kinsmen', or an irregular reading (qira'a shadha) that he narrated. Al-Isma'ili said: Ibn Abbas recited it."]].

Al-Malihi, Abd al-Wahid ibn Ahmad, informed us; al-Nu'aymi, Ahmad ibn Abd Allah, informed us; Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us; Muhammad ibn Isma'il (al-Bukhari) narrated to us; Umar ibn Hafs ibn Ghiyath narrated to us; my father (Hafs ibn Ghiyath) narrated to us; al-A'mash narrated to us; Amr ibn Murrah narrated to me, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, who said: When the verse ﴿And warn your nearest kinsmen﴾ was revealed, the Prophet (ﷺ) ascended al-Safa and began calling out: "O sons of Fihr! O sons of Adi!" (referring to the clans of Quraysh) until they gathered. A man who could not come out would send a messenger to see what it was. Abu Lahab and Quraysh came, and he said: "Tell me, if I informed you that cavalry in the valley were about to raid you, would you believe me?" They said: "Yes, we have never found from you anything but truth." He said: "Then I am a warner to you before a severe punishment." Abu Lahab said: "Destruction to you all day! Did you gather us only for this?" Then the following was revealed: "Perish the hands of Abu Lahab, and perish he. His wealth will not avail him, nor what he earned."

[[Narrated by al-Bukhari in the tafsir of the surah al-Shu'ara', chapter: "And warn your nearest kinsmen", 8 / 501, and in the surah Tabbat, 8 / 737; and by Muslim in Iman: 1 / 194. Al-A'mash did not mention the revelation of the verse in the narration.]]

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 26, verse 215:

Abdul-Wahid al-Maliḥi informed us, Ahmad ibn Abdullah al-Nu'aymi informed us, Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us, Muhammad ibn Isma'il (al-Bukhari) related to us, Abu al-Yaman related to us, Shu'ayb informed us, from al-Zuhri, who said: Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib and Abu Salama ibn Abd al-Rahman informed me that Abu Hurayrah said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) stood up when God Most High revealed: ﴿And warn your closest kinsmen﴾. He said: "O assembly of Quraysh, or words to that effect, buy yourselves back; I cannot avail you anything against God. O Banu Abd Manaf, I cannot avail you anything against God. O Abbas ibn Abd al-Muttalib, I cannot avail you anything against God. O Safiyyah, aunt of the Messenger of God, I cannot avail you anything against God. And O Fatimah, daughter of Muhammad, ask me for whatever you wish of my wealth; I cannot avail you anything against God."

[Narrated by al-Bukhari in the Tafsir of the surah "Tabbat" (8/501-502), and in the Wasaya and al-Anbiya', and by Muslim in al-Iman (1/192-193), and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah (13/329).]

Abu Sa'id Abdullah ibn Ahmad al-Tahiri informed us, my grandfather Abu Sahl ibn Abd al-Samad ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Bazzaz informed me, Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Zakariyya al-Adhafiri informed us, Ishaq ibn Ibrahim al-Dabari informed us, Abd al-Razzaq related to us, Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah, from Mutarrif ibn Abdullah ibn al-Shikhkhir, from Iyad ibn Himar al-Mujashi'i, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "God, Mighty and Majestic, has commanded me to teach you what you do not know of what He taught me this day. He said: Every wealth that I have granted to My servants is lawful for them. I created My servants as hanifs (upright in faith), all of them, but the devils came to them and led them astray from their religion, and forbade them what I had made lawful for them, and commanded them to associate with Me that for which I have sent down no authority. God looked upon the people of the earth and despised them, Arab and non-Arab, except for remnants of the People of the Book. God, Most High, commanded me to warn Quraysh. I said: O Lord, if I do, they will crush my head until they leave it like a piece of bread. He said: I have sent you only to test you and to test others through you. I have sent down to you a Book which water cannot wash away; you will recite it in sleep and in wakefulness. So fight them, and We shall aid you; spend, and We shall spend upon you; send an army, and We shall reinforce you with five times as many; and fight with those who obey you against those who disobey you." Then he said: "The people of Paradise are three: a just ruler; a merciful, tender-hearted man towards every near relative and every Muslim; and a wealthy man who gives charity. The people of Hell are five: the weak one who has no religion, who follow you without seeking family or wealth; a man who, in the morning or evening, deceives you concerning your family and your wealth; a man who does not let go of any greed, however small, without seizing it; and the foul-mouthed, obscene person." He said: And he mentioned stinginess and lying.

[Narrated by Abd al-Razzaq in his Musannaf, within his transmission of the Jami' of Imam Ma'mar ibn Rashid (11/120-121); by Muslim in al-Jannah wa Sifat Na'imiha, chapter on the qualities by which the people of Paradise and the people of Hell are known in this world, no. 2865 (4/2197-2198); and by the author in Sharh al-Sunnah (14/407-408).]

God, Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿And lower your wing to those among the believers who follow you﴾.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 26, verses 216–220:

﴿And if they disobey you, then say: "Indeed, I am free of what you do."﴾ — of disbelief and the worship of other than Allah.

﴿And put your trust﴾ — Ahl al-Madina and al-Sham read it as "fa-tawakkal" with the fa' (fa'), and so it is in their codices. The rest read it with the waw, "wa-tawakkal." ﴿in the Mighty, the Merciful﴾ — so that He will suffice you against the plots of the enemies.

﴿Who sees you when you stand﴾ — to your prayer, according to most of the exegetes. Mujahid said: "Who sees you wherever you are." It was also said: "when you stand" for calling them (to Islam).

﴿And your movement among those who prostrate﴾ — that is: He sees your movement in your prayer, in your standing, bowing, prostrating and sitting. 'Ikrimah and 'Atiyyah narrated from Ibn 'Abbas: "among those who prostrate" means "among those who pray." Muqatil and al-Kalbi said: that is, with those who pray in congregation. It means: He sees you when you stand alone for prayer, and He sees you when you pray with those praying in congregation. Mujahid said: He sees the turning of your gaze among those who pray, for he would see from behind him as he sees from in front of him. Abu al-Hasan al-Sarakhsi informed us, Zahir ibn Ahmad informed us, Abu Ishaq al-Hashimi informed us, Abu Mus'ab informed us, from Malik, from Abu al-Zinad, from al-A'raj, from Abu Hurayrah that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Do you see my qibla here? By Allah, your humility and your bowing are not hidden from me. Indeed, I see you from behind my back."[[Narrated by Malik in al-Muwatta', Book of Shortening the Prayer during Travel, Chapter on Action in Prayer: 1/167; al-Bukhari in the Book of Prayer, Chapter on the Imam's Admonition Regarding Completing the Prayer: 1/514; Muslim in the Book of Prayer, Chapter on the Command to Perfect the Prayer, no. (424): 1/319; and al-Musannif in Sharh al-Sunnah: 13/289.]] Al-Hasan said: "And your movement among those who prostrate" means your conduct, your going and your coming among your believing companions. Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: it means your conduct in your affairs, as the prophets before you were. "Those who prostrate" are the prophets. 'Ata' narrated from Ibn 'Abbas: he meant your movement through the loins of the prophets, from one prophet to another, until He brought you forth in this ummah.[[Mentioned these sayings: al-Tabari: 19/123–125; al-Suyuti: 6/331–332; Ibn al-Jawzi: 6/148–149. Al-Tabari preferred that the most correct of the sayings in interpreting the verse is that it means: He sees your movement together with those who prostrate in their prayer with you, when you stand with them and bow and prostrate, because that is the apparent meaning of it.]]

﴿Indeed, it is He who is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing.﴾

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 26, verse 221–225:

﴿Shall I inform you﴾ (hal unabbi'ukum), i.e., "shall I tell you", ﴿upon whom the devils descend?﴾ This is the answer to their saying: "A devil has descended upon him." Then He explained, saying: ﴿They descend﴾, i.e., they keep descending, ﴿upon every lying﴾ (affak), i.e., liar, ﴿sinful﴾ (athim), i.e., wicked. Qatadah said: "They are the soothsayers (kahanah). The jinn steal the hearing, then they convey it to their allies among mankind." This is His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿They cast the hearing﴾ ﴿They cast the hearing﴾, i.e., they listen from the angels while stationed, then they convey it to the soothsayers. ﴿And most of them are liars﴾, because they mix a great deal of falsehood into it.

His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿As for the poets, the deviators follow them﴾. The people of tafsir said: He meant the poets of the disbelievers who used to satirize the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. Muqatil mentioned their names, saying: among them were ʿAbdullah ibn al-Zibaʿra al-Sahmi, Hubayrah ibn Abi Wahb al-Makhzumi, Mushafi' ibn ʿAbd Manaf, Abu ʿIzzah ibn ʿAbdullah al-Jumahi, and Umayyah ibn Abi al-Salt al-Thaqafi. They spoke falsehood and untruth, and said: "We say the same as what Muhammad says." They composed poetry, and there gathered around them deviators from their people who would listen to their poems when they satirized the Prophet ﷺ and his companions, and they would transmit them from them. This is the meaning of: ﴿As for the poets, the deviators follow them﴾, meaning they are the transmitters who narrate the satire of the Prophet ﷺ and the Muslims. Qatadah and Mujahid said: "The deviators (al-ghawun) are the devils." Al-Dahhak said: Two men were reviling each other during the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, one of them from the Ansar and the other from another tribe, and with each of them were deviators from his people, who were the foolish ones, so this verse was revealed. This is the narration of ʿAtiyyah from Ibn ʿAbbas (ibn ʿAbbas).

﴿Do you not see that they wander in every valley﴾ [of the valleys of speech] ﴿wandering﴾, i.e., going astray and deviating from the path of truth. The hayim is one who goes off aimlessly with no destination.

Ibn ʿAbbas (radiyallahu ʿanhuma) said regarding this verse: "In every idle talk they plunge." Mujahid said: "In every art they cause confusion." Qatadah said: "They praise with falsehood, and they listen and satirize with falsehood." Thus "valley" is a metaphor for the various kinds of speech, as one says: "I am in one valley and you are in another." It has also been said: "In every valley they wander" means: on every letter of the alphabet they fashion rhymes.
