**Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 26, verses 226–227:**

﴿And that they say what they do not do﴾. That is: they lie in their poetry. They say, "We did this and we did that," but they are liars. Abu Muhammad Abd al-Wahid al-Malihi informed us, Abu Muhammad Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Shurayh informed us, Abu al-Qasim al-Baghawi informed us, Ali ibn al-Ja'd related to us, Shu'bah informed us from al-A'mash, from Dhakwan, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "For one of you to have his belly filled with pus is better for him than for it to be filled with poetry."[[Narrated by al-Bukhari in al-Adab, chapter "What is disliked of a person being preoccupied with poetry to the point that it keeps him from the remembrance of Allah, knowledge and the Qur'an": 10/548; and Muslim in the Book of Poetry, no. (2257): 4/1769; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 12/380.]] Then He excepted the poets of the Muslims who used to respond to the poets of the Jahiliyyah (the pre-Islamic Age of Ignorance), satirize the poets of the disbelievers, and defend the Prophet (ﷺ) and his Companions. Among them were Hassan ibn Thabit, Abdullah ibn Rawahah, and Ka'b ibn Malik. So He said: ﴿Except those who believe and do righteous deeds﴾. Ahmad ibn Abdullah al-Salihi informed us, Abu al-Husayn Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Bishran informed us, Isma'il ibn Muhammad al-Saffar informed us, Ahmad ibn Mansur al-Ramadi related to us, Abd al-Razzaq related to us, Ma'mar informed us from al-Zuhri, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Ka'b ibn Malik, from his father, that he said to the Prophet (ﷺ): "Allah has revealed concerning poetry what He has revealed." The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Indeed the believer strives with his sword and his tongue. By Him in whose hand is my soul, it is as if you are shooting them with arrows."[[Narrated by Abd al-Razzaq in the Kitab al-Jami': 11/263; Ibn Hibban authenticated it, p. (494) of Mawarid al-Zam'an; al-Bayhaqi in al-Sunan: 10/239; Imam Ahmad in al-Musnad: 3/456, 460, and 6/387. The author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 12/378. Ibn Hajar in al-Kafi al-Shaf, p. (123), and al-Manawi in Fath al-Samawi: 2/889, attributed it to Ibn Sa'd in al-Tabaqat, and it was attributed in al-Matalib al-Aliyah: 3/354, 355 to Abu Ya'la. See: al-Albani's Silsilat al-Ahadith al-Sahihah, no. (1631).]].

Abdullah ibn Abd al-Samad al-Jawzajani informed us, Abu al-Qasim Ali ibn Ahmad al-Khuza'i informed us, al-Haytham ibn Kulayb informed us, Abu Isa al-Tirmidhi informed us, Ishaq ibn Mansur related to us, Abd al-Razzaq informed us, Ja'far ibn Sulayman informed us, Thabit related to us, from Anas, that the Prophet (ﷺ) entered Makkah during the Umrat al-Qada' (the make-up pilgrimage), while Ibn Rawahah was walking in front of him and saying:

"Clear the way for the sons of the disbelievers away from his path... Today we shall strike you for his revelation,

A blow that removes the skull from its resting place... and makes a close friend forget his close friend."

Umar said to him: "O son of Rawahah, in front of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and in the sanctuary of Allah you recite poetry?" The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Leave him alone, O Umar, for it is swifter against them than the shooting of arrows."[[Narrated by al-Tirmidhi in al-Adab, chapter "What has come concerning the recitation of poetry": 8/138–140, and he said: "This is a hasan gharib sahih hadith from this route. Abd al-Razzaq also narrated this hadith from Ma'mar from al-Zuhri, in a different hadith, that the Prophet (ﷺ) entered Makkah during the Umrat al-Qada', with Ka'b ibn Malik before him. This is more authentic according to some hadith scholars, because Abdullah ibn Rawahah was killed on the day of Mu'tah, and the Umrat al-Qada' took place after that." It was also narrated by him in his separate work al-Shama'il al-Muhammadiyyah, p. (145); by al-Nasa'i in al-Manasik, chapter "Reciting poetry in the sanctuary...": 2/25–26; by Abu Nu'aym in al-Hilyah: 6/292; and by the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 12/374. See: Fath al-Bari: 7/502; al-Albani's Silsilat al-Ahadith al-Sahihah, no. (593).]]

Abd al-Wahid al-Malihi informed us, Ahmad ibn Abdullah al-Nu'aymi informed us, Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us, Muhammad ibn Isma'il related to us, Hajjaj ibn Minhal related to us, Shu'bah related to us, Adi informed me that he heard al-Bara' say: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to Hassan: "Satirize them, or satirize them, and Jibril is with you."[[Narrated by al-Bukhari in Bad' al-Khalq, chapter "Mention of the angels": 6/304; in al-Maghazi: 7/416; and in al-Adab: 10/546; and Muslim in Fada'il al-Sahabah, chapter "Virtues of Hassan," no. (2486): 4/1933; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 12/377.]]

Abdullah ibn Abd al-Samad al-Jawzajani informed us, Abu al-Qasim al-Khuza'i informed us, al-Haytham ibn Kulayb informed us, Abu Isa related to us, Isma'il ibn Musa al-Fazari and Ali ibn Hujr related to us, with the meaning being one, and they both said: Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi al-Zinad related to us, from Hisham ibn Urwah, from his father, from Aishah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) would set up a pulpit for Hassan ibn Thabit in the mosque, upon which he would stand and boast on behalf of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), or defend the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed Allah supports Hassan with the Ruh al-Qudus (the Holy Spirit) as long as he defends or boasts on behalf of the Messenger of Allah."[[Narrated by al-Tirmidhi in al-Adab, chapter "What has come concerning the recitation of poetry": 8/137, and he said: "This is a hasan gharib sahih hadith." It was also narrated in al-Shama'il, p. (147); authenticated by al-Hakim: 3/487; and by the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 12/377. See also: al-Albani's Silsilat al-Ahadith al-Sahihah: 3/177.]]

Isma'il ibn Abd al-Qahir informed us, Abd al-Ghaffar ibn Muhammad informed us, Muhammad ibn Isa al-Juludi related to us, Ibrahim ibn Muhammad ibn Sufyan related to us, Muslim ibn al-Hajjaj related to us, Abd al-Malik ibn Shu'ayb ibn al-Layth related to us, my father related to me from my grandfather, Khalid ibn Zayd related to us, Sa'id ibn Abi Hilal related to me from Umarah ibn Ghaziyyah, from Muhammad ibn Ibrahim, from Abi, from Salamah ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Aishah, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Satirize the Quraysh, for it is more painful to them than a volley of arrows." So he sent for Ibn Rawahah and said: "Satirize them." He satirized them, but it did not satisfy him. So he sent for Ka'b ibn Malik, then he sent for Hassan ibn Thabit. When he entered upon him, Hassan said: "The time has come for you to send for this lion that strikes with its tail," then he stuck out his tongue and began to move it, and said: "By the One who sent you with the truth, I will tear them apart with my tongue as a hide is torn." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Do not hasten. Abu Bakr is the most knowledgeable of the Quraysh about their lineages, and I have a lineage among them, until your lineage is clarified for you." Hassan went to him and then returned, and said: "O Messenger of Allah, your lineage has been clarified for me. By the One who sent you with the truth, I will pluck you out from among them as a hair is plucked from dough." Aishah said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say to Hassan: "Indeed the Ruh al-Qudus will continue to support you as long as you defend Allah and His Messenger." She also said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "Satirize them, Hassan, and he has healed and been healed." Hassan said:

"You satirized Muhammad, so I responded on his behalf, and with Allah is the recompense for that.

You satirized Muhammad, the pious, upright one, the Messenger of Allah, whose nature is fidelity.

Indeed my father, my mother, and my honor are a shield for the honor of Muhammad from you.

Whoever among you satirizes the Messenger of Allah, and whoever praises and supports him, are equal.

Jibril is the Messenger of Allah among us, and the Ruh al-Qudus has no equal."[[Narrated by Muslim in Fada'il al-Sahabah, chapter "Virtues of Hassan," no. (2490): 4/1935–1938; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 10/25.]]

Abd al-Wahid al-Malihi informed us, Ahmad ibn Abdullah al-Nu'aymi informed us, Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us, Muhammad ibn Isma'il related to us, Abu al-Yaman related to us, Shu'ayb informed us from al-Zuhri, Abu Bakr ibn Abd al-Rahman informed me that Marwan ibn al-Hakam informed him that Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Aswad ibn Abd Yaghuth informed him that Ubayy ibn Ka'b informed him that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed, some poetry is wisdom."[[Narrated by al-Bukhari in al-Adab, chapter "What is permissible of poetry and rajaz": 10/537; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 12/369.]] Aishah, may Allah be pleased with her, said: "Poetry is speech; some of it is good and some of it is bad. So take the good and leave the bad."[[See: Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 13/150.]] Al-Sha'bi said: Abu Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, used to recite poetry, Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, used to recite poetry, and Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, was the most poetic of the three.[[See al-Musannaf of Ibn Abi Shaybah: 8/698.]]

It was narrated from Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, that he used to recite poetry in the mosque and ask others to recite it to him. It is related that he called Umar ibn Abi Rabi'ah al-Makhzumi and asked him to recite the qasidah (ode) that he had composed, which begins: "Are you departing at dawn from the family of Nu'm, or going at noon in the heat?"

Ibn Abi Rabi'ah recited the ode to its end, and it is about seventy verses. Then Ibn Abbas repeated the entire ode, having memorized it after only one hearing.

﴿And they remember Allah often﴾. That is: poetry did not distract them from the remembrance of Allah. ﴿And they defended themselves after they had been wronged﴾. Muqatil said: They defended themselves against the polytheists, because the polytheists began with satire. Then He threatened the poets of the polytheists, saying: ﴿And those who did wrong will know﴾, that is, those who associated partners with Allah and satirized the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ),[[It was said that those meant are the people of Makkah, and it was said: those who did wrong among the polytheists. The correct view is that this verse is general for every wrongdoer. See: Tafsir Ibn Kathir: 3/356.]] ﴿by what return they will be returned﴾, that is, to what place of return they will be returned after death. Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, said: To Jahannam and the Sa'ir (blazing fire). And Allah knows best.[[A portion of a hadith previously cited, narrated by al-Bukhari in al-Nikah: 9/104, and Muslim in al-Nikah also: 2/1020.]]

**Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 26, verses 226–227:**

﴿And that they say what they do not do﴾. That is: they lie in their poetry. They say, "We did this and we did that," but they are liars. Abu Muhammad Abd al-Wahid al-Malihi informed us, Abu Muhammad Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Shurayh informed us, Abu al-Qasim al-Baghawi informed us, Ali ibn al-Ja'd related to us, Shu'bah informed us from al-A'mash, from Dhakwan, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "For one of you to have his belly filled with pus is better for him than for it to be filled with poetry."[[Narrated by al-Bukhari in al-Adab, chapter "What is disliked of a person being preoccupied with poetry to the point that it keeps him from the remembrance of Allah, knowledge and the Qur'an": 10/548; and Muslim in the Book of Poetry, no. (2257): 4/1769; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 12/380.]] Then He excepted the poets of the Muslims who used to respond to the poets of the Jahiliyyah (the pre-Islamic Age of Ignorance), satirize the poets of the disbelievers, and defend the Prophet (ﷺ) and his Companions. Among them were Hassan ibn Thabit, Abdullah ibn Rawahah, and Ka'b ibn Malik. So He said: ﴿Except those who believe and do righteous deeds﴾. Ahmad ibn Abdullah al-Salihi informed us, Abu al-Husayn Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Bishran informed us, Isma'il ibn Muhammad al-Saffar informed us, Ahmad ibn Mansur al-Ramadi related to us, Abd al-Razzaq related to us, Ma'mar informed us from al-Zuhri, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Ka'b ibn Malik, from his father, that he said to the Prophet (ﷺ): "Allah has revealed concerning poetry what He has revealed." The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Indeed the believer strives with his sword and his tongue. By Him in whose hand is my soul, it is as if you are shooting them with arrows."[[Narrated by Abd al-Razzaq in the Kitab al-Jami': 11/263; Ibn Hibban authenticated it, p. (494) of Mawarid al-Zam'an; al-Bayhaqi in al-Sunan: 10/239; Imam Ahmad in al-Musnad: 3/456, 460, and 6/387. The author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 12/378. Ibn Hajar in al-Kafi al-Shaf, p. (123), and al-Manawi in Fath al-Samawi: 2/889, attributed it to Ibn Sa'd in al-Tabaqat, and it was attributed in al-Matalib al-Aliyah: 3/354, 355 to Abu Ya'la. See: al-Albani's Silsilat al-Ahadith al-Sahihah, no. (1631).]].

Abdullah ibn Abd al-Samad al-Jawzajani informed us, Abu al-Qasim Ali ibn Ahmad al-Khuza'i informed us, al-Haytham ibn Kulayb informed us, Abu Isa al-Tirmidhi informed us, Ishaq ibn Mansur related to us, Abd al-Razzaq informed us, Ja'far ibn Sulayman informed us, Thabit related to us, from Anas, that the Prophet (ﷺ) entered Makkah during the Umrat al-Qada' (the make-up pilgrimage), while Ibn Rawahah was walking in front of him and saying:

"Clear the way for the sons of the disbelievers away from his path... Today we shall strike you for his revelation,

A blow that removes the skull from its resting place... and makes a close friend forget his close friend."

Umar said to him: "O son of Rawahah, in front of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and in the sanctuary of Allah you recite poetry?" The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Leave him alone, O Umar, for it is swifter against them than the shooting of arrows."[[Narrated by al-Tirmidhi in al-Adab, chapter "What has come concerning the recitation of poetry": 8/138–140, and he said: "This is a hasan gharib sahih hadith from this route. Abd al-Razzaq also narrated this hadith from Ma'mar from al-Zuhri, in a different hadith, that the Prophet (ﷺ) entered Makkah during the Umrat al-Qada', with Ka'b ibn Malik before him. This is more authentic according to some hadith scholars, because Abdullah ibn Rawahah was killed on the day of Mu'tah, and the Umrat al-Qada' took place after that." It was also narrated by him in his separate work al-Shama'il al-Muhammadiyyah, p. (145); by al-Nasa'i in al-Manasik, chapter "Reciting poetry in the sanctuary...": 2/25–26; by Abu Nu'aym in al-Hilyah: 6/292; and by the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 12/374.
